newsitem.title: UK: Oil prices end year firm as European winter bites.
newsitem.headline: Oil prices end year firm as European winter bites.

text.p: World oil prices edged higher on Tuesday to end the year on a strong footing, supported by a blast of cold weather in Europe which boosted demand for heating fuel.
London February futures for bellwether North Sea Brent Blend crude gained 12 cents to close at $23.80 a barrel, nearly $5.50 a barrel up from the start of the year.
Gas oil (heating oil) futures set the pace again, consolidating Monday's rally prompted by the cold snap which could continue at least until the end of the week, leading crude oil markets higher.
"With most of Europe in the grip of severe winter weather, gas oil led the way higher," said brokers MeesPierson in a daily report.
The arctic conditions have caused transport chaos across Europe, claimed at least 90 lives and dumped snow on the Mediterranean island of Corsica.
January gas oil futures in London closed 75 cents a tonne firmer at $223.50.
For the oil market, the year ends much as it began with weather forecasts again the focus of traders' calculations.

At the start of 1996, blizzards in the north eastern states of the United States, the world's single largest heating oil market, pushed crude values up before Spring talk of an agreement to allow Baghdad to sell oil for the first time since the Gulf War pushed them back again.
Despite the United Nations oil-for-food deal, finally implemented on December 17, the average price of a barrel of Brent over the year -- at $20.32 -- is running about 20 percent higher than in 1995.
Strong support has come from a widespread western oil company policy of cutting costs by keeping inventory levels as low as possible, reducing insulation to supply disruptions or increased demand.

Germany, easily Europe's biggest heating oil consumer, has been running on unusually thin inventories this winter, leaving prices vulnerable to the surge in consumption provoked by some of the most severe winter weather seen in a decade.
German household stocks of heating oil fell in November to about 62 percent of capacity, compared with 68 percent last year, German traders have estimated.

Unseasonally mild weather in the past few days in the northeastern states of the United States, has acted as a brake on the price in the last few days but colder weather in the New Year could prompt a further rally, given the depleted stocks.
Data released last week showed a hefty 5-6 million barrel weekly fall in U.S. crude oil stocks levels, to around 290 million barrels.
U.S. stocks of heating oil also fell by 1.5-2 million barrels. While this is a relatively small amount, it had a positive effect on prices because traders had been expecting a rise..
Oil markets so far have found little difficulty in absorbing the limited volumes of Iraqi oil exports permitted under the U.N. oil-for-food exchange.

Iraq started exports earlier this month under one of 21 contracts for some 500,000 barrels a day of crude sales, enough at current prices to raise the $2 billion Iraq is allowed over a six-month period to pay for humanitarian needs.
